speedrun: Inventory the repository and locate the executable, Python runner, SQL migrations, views, fixtures, and benchmark scripts.
Read `./incident-report` and identify its argument handling, database setup, and report-writing path.
Inspect the repository tree for operations notes, documented TSV columns, and shard configuration.
Read the ingestion and decoder-wrapper Python modules.
Read the SQL schema, migrations, compatibility views, query fragments, and aggregation code.
Locate every call site of `bin/wire-decode` and determine whether decoding is per-record or batched.
Run the visible fixture through `./incident-report` and save its current TSV output.
Run the included benchmark to establish the current throughput and failure mode.
Read the local wire-decoder operations note and inspect `bin/wire-decode` usage behavior.
Construct a small probe JSONL containing one-field records for each modality and run the decoder.
Probe signed, zero, maximum, reordered-tag, duplicate-sequence, and stream-transition cases.
Probe malformed records and verify whether decoder state changes after them.
Inspect the SQLite schema and existing shard/view contents at modality and status boundaries.
Patch the decoder wrapper to implement or batch the characterized decode behavior once per stream/input batch.
Patch parsing so malformed lines are skipped without terminating or corrupting decoder state.
Patch the compatibility view to retain error rows and expose every relevant modality.
Replace shard-specific filtering with one set-based union over all configured shards.
Materialize a normalized event relation before report aggregation.
Apply stream-local modality-aware duplicate suppression before aggregation.
Fix the aggregation joins so counters, synthetic checks, spans, and sampled logs all survive.
Implement the repository's deterministic percentile rank rule and error/zero-duration handling.
Run Python syntax checks and SQLite query/migration checks.
Re-run the checked-in fixture and verify TSV schema, ordering, and deterministic output.
Generate a small adversarial stream with all modalities, malformed lines, duplicates, boundaries, and interleaved streams.
Run the report on that stream and inspect totals, errors, unique traces, and percentile fields.
Run the 100,000-event benchmark and profile or optimize any remaining subprocess or per-row overhead.
Run shard-boundary and timestamp-boundary cases, then repeat the benchmark and final fixture comparison.
invalid_failure_risks: The repository may not document the exact TSV schema, percentile rank rule, or normalization semantics sufficiently for an agent to determine the required behavior from the supplied description alone.
The compiled decoder may not expose enough observable behavior to infer all hidden wire encodings, especially if hidden generation uses cases not represented by the operations note or probes.
A fixed 30,000-events-per-second threshold on a one-CPU container can be flaky due to host load, filesystem behavior, SQLite configuration, or process startup variance.
The benchmark input shape and startup grace period are not specified precisely, so equivalent implementations could receive different measured throughput.
The stated 99.5% cell criterion is potentially inconsistent with tests that appear to require exact behavior for particular boundary and percentile cases.
If the supplied binary or shared library is architecture-dependent or not actually present in the image, the task becomes invalid independently of the solver's changes.
review.reasons: The task has a clear operational end state and a strong deterministic hidden-test strategy covering the planted failure modes, while the opaque decoder, cross-layer refactor, and throughput requirement create genuine engineering difficulty. It is realistic for an incident repair, although the combination of reverse engineering, SQL redesign, and performance work makes the under-one-hour solvability marginal rather than easy.
fixes: Document the exact existing TSV columns, ordering, percentile rank rule, and normalized event semantics in a local repository file or test oracle.
Specify the benchmark command, input shape, startup grace period, and acceptable measurement procedure to reduce performance flakiness.
Provide a local probe generator or independent reference checker for the wire decoder so all required behaviors are experimentally distinguishable without relying on hidden assumptions.
Clarify whether hidden verification requires exact report equality or permits the stated 99.5% cell threshold, and align the tests with one policy.
Explicitly state the supported CPU architecture and verify that the compiled decoder and shared library are included in the built image.

verdicts.reason: The candidate reconstructs deterministic SQLite event rollups from JSONL using sharded tables and a wire decoder, whereas the reference replays incident databases with alias resolution, dependency ordering, corrections, and SLA state materialization.
The candidate reports telemetry event aggregates and modalities, while the reference validates cryptographically authenticated audit chains and emits authoritative events.
The candidate repairs JSONL-to-TSV event aggregation, whereas the reference replays committed transactional shards into canonical live-row JSON and validates deployment checksums.
The candidate performs telemetry rollups with malformed-line tolerance, while the reference reconciles authenticated binary financial settlement frames and signed adjustments.
The candidate computes event reports from telemetry data, whereas the reference authorizes SQL statements against SQLite policy state with per-request decisions and performance constraints.
